answer: Each identity anchors at a jetty berth, locks a 60-credit bond, and emits a signal the jetty receiver measures. Farther berths weaken the signal, so each identity pays a distance fee: the first berth 30 credits, the k-th 30+4(k-1) credits. A thousand fake identities lock 60,000 credits and pay 2,028,000, the thousandth 4,026. A rented-amplifier ring fails: each amplifier serial is key-bound to one berth anchor, and the receiver checks strength against the distance table; a mismatch burns the bond. An honest agent pays one bond and a 30-credit fee, and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
